strengths: Practical motivation addressing real bottleneck in indoor occupancy learning (NYUv2 has only 1,449 images); scalable YouTube harvesting pipeline with automatic camera parameter extraction via Dust3R is practical and novel as first application to occupancy prediction

Comprehensive experimental validation across two benchmarks (NYUv2, OccScanNet) with evaluation at multiple annotation percentages (1%-100%); strong improvements in low-data regimes (+5.25% mIoU at 10% labels) demonstrating pre-training utility
Well-motivated design for indoor scenes: superpixel/supervoxel representation appropriately reduces pixel-level noise and focuses on object-level semantics relevant to cluttered environments

Adequate implementation details (optimizer, learning rates, hardware) support reproducibility of fine-tuning experiments; proper experimental setup (scene-level split in OccScanNet prevents data leakage)
Honest discussion of limitations including non-public dataset and unhandled dynamic objects; addresses societal impacts of using internet data
weaknesses: Critical limitation: Authors explicitly state the YouTube-Occ dataset 'will not be released in public' (Section 6), which fundamentally undermines a claimed dataset contribution. Without public access, the community cannot verify quality, reproducibility is compromised, and practical adoption is severely limited. Privacy justification is not adequately detailed.

Insufficient validation of automatic label quality: no quantitative assessment of Dust3R camera accuracy or depth reliability in complex indoor scenes; no validation of semantic labels from off-the-shelf SAN model; no analysis of how label noise propagates; simple majority voting for supervoxel assignment is ad-hoc and potentially problematic with ambiguous semantics

Lack of statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance testing despite claiming SOTA. Improvements are often modest (NYUv2: +1.04% mIoU, +1.21% IoU; OccScanNet: +0.30% mIoU, +0.25% IoU) and may be within noise. Single run reported—no discussion of variance across random seeds.

Limited methodological novelty: pre-training approach combines established techniques (superpixels, VFM-based distillation, contrastive loss). The specific application to occupancy prediction is incremental. Critical ablations missing: why superpixels over alternatives? sensitivity to temperature τ_sp? optimal number of superpixels?

Dataset quality concerns: 14,592 frames from 651 clips is modest compared to modern standards (OccScanNet: 45,755 training images). Very poor zero-shot performance (9.95% mIoU on NYUv2, 4.61% on OccScanNet) indicates substantial domain gap, questioning pre-training utility. No dataset analysis of diversity, class balance, or failure modes.

Technical assumptions lack validation: wall height fixed at 2.8m is not universal and could incorrectly scale scenes with variable ceiling heights; Dust3R depth reliability in textureless indoor regions not validated; cascading errors from inaccurate depth and camera parameters not analyzed.

Insufficient ablation studies and analysis: no ablation on superpixel generation, loss variants, or VFM choices; limited per-class performance analysis; improvements diminish with more labeled data, suggesting either dataset noise or limited method benefit beyond low-data regimes; no visualization of learned representations or failure cases.

Marginal qualitative improvements: Figures 3 and 4 show subtle visual differences between proposed method and Symphonies baseline, raising questions about practical significance of numerical gains despite claims of SOTA.

strengths: Addresses real problem of data scarcity for indoor 3D scene understanding by leveraging freely available internet data
Presents complete end-to-end pipeline for automated processing of YouTube videos without camera parameters (Dust3R + semantic labeling)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including cross-dataset pre-training and annotation-efficient learning across multiple label percentages
Consistent improvements shown across different data regimes with larger gains at lower label percentages (+5.25% mIoU at 10% labels on NYUv2)
Intuitive approach to region-level semantic matching via superpixel-supervoxel correspondence
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: straightforward application of VFM superpixels + standard contrastive distillation loss without architectural innovation
Dataset not released publicly ('will not be released in public'), severely undermining reproducibility and eliminating value as a dataset contribution

Reconstruction quality unverified: no quantitative assessment of Dust3R accuracy on internet videos with motion blur and handheld camera movement; semantic labels from SAN introduce unquantified noise
Modest empirical improvements lack statistical validation: NYUv2 +1.04% mIoU, OccScanNet +0.30% mIoU with no error bars, confidence intervals, or multiple runs reported
Zero-shot performance critically contradicts main claims: only 9.95% mIoU on NYUv2 and 4.61% on OccScanNet, suggesting learned features are dataset-specific rather than generalizable
Missing critical ablation studies: no ablations on superpixel method, pixel vs. region-level distillation, or individual component contributions
Questionable preprocessing assumptions: arbitrary 2.8m wall height for metric scaling with no validation or sensitivity analysis; z-up alignment correctness unverified
Poor transfer learning: dramatic improvement decline with increasing labeled data (Table 4: +2.47% at 1% → +0.06% at 50%) indicates weak domain transfer
Unaddressed dynamic objects: house tour videos contain people and moving furniture but paper dismisses this as future work without impact analysis
No comparative evaluation: lacks comparison with other web-data learning approaches or self-supervised 3D methods beyond baseline

strengths: Addresses a practical problem (scarcity of large-scale indoor 3D data) with a pragmatic web-based solution
Comprehensive and thorough experimental validation across multiple data regimes (full, 50%, 10% annotations) and benchmarks (NYUv2, OccScanNet)
Fully automated, scalable pipeline that achieves metric-scale 3D reconstruction without pre-calibrated cameras, demonstrating practical feasibility
Consistent improvements across diverse annotation percentages, showing robustness of pre-training approach, particularly beneficial for low-data regimes (5.25% gain at 10% NYUv2 labels)
Well-motivated use of superpixel-supervoxel alignment to handle object-level complexity in indoor scenes, avoiding pixel-level noise and scale variability issues
Clear presentation with effective visualizations of the pipeline and experimental results
Adequate implementation details and reproducibility information for the methodology component
weaknesses: Critical limitation: YouTube-Occ dataset will not be released publicly, severely undermining the dataset contribution and preventing community verification, extension, and reproducibility
Incremental performance improvements (1.04% mIoU on NYUv2, 0.30% on OccScanNet) are modest; improvements at high baseline performance may not justify methodological complexity

Limited technical novelty in the pre-training method; superpixel-supervoxel contrastive distillation applies existing concepts straightforwardly without clear distinction from prior self-supervised 3D work (CrossPoint, MM-Point)
Insufficient ablation studies: no pixel vs. superpixel comparison, no sensitivity to superpixel parameters, no justification for VFM choice (SAN), no component importance analysis
Dataset quality and filtering metrics absent: percentage of frames retained after filtering unknown, Dust3R reconstruction errors not quantified, semantic labeling quality from SAN not evaluated
Domain gap inadequately addressed: zero-shot performance extremely low (9.95% NYUv2, 4.61% OccScanNet), indicating substantial unresolved domain mismatch between YouTube and benchmark distributions
No statistical rigor: acknowledged lack of error bars, single runs without variance reporting, no confidence intervals or significance tests on reported improvements
Acknowledged limitation on handling dynamic objects not addressed; real indoor scenes contain people and moving furniture, limiting practical applicability
Privacy concerns in house tour videos (identifiable people, household details, addresses) are underexplored despite being a sensitive dataset collection issue

Missing technical details: superpixel generation algorithm and parameters not specified, majority voting for voxel-superpixel conflicts inadequately explained, Dust3R post-processing thresholds not provided

strengths: Novel problem formulation: First work to leverage uncalibrated YouTube videos for indoor occupancy prediction, addressing data scarcity and privacy concerns with a practical, scalable solution
Well-motivated pre-training framework: Clear demonstration (Sec 5.2) that naive pseudo-label supervision fails, justifying the distillation-based approach rather than direct supervision

Comprehensive experimental validation: Evaluates across three diverse architectures (CNN, Transformer, Gaussian-based) showing model-agnostic benefits; consistent improvements on NYUv2 and Occ-ScanNet; strong few-shot results (+3.29% at 5% labels)
Practical data pipeline: Clever use of real estate footage with stable motion; integration of foundation models (Dust3R, SAN); 100K+ frames across 5K scenes; commitment to public release
Thorough ablations and analysis: Tables 5-6 examine loss components and design choices; qualitative visualizations support claims; baseline comparisons provided
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Voxel-anchored Gaussianization is straightforward (fixed scale/rotation); class-prototype learning and region-level alignment are standard techniques; framework primarily assembles existing components without significant algorithmic innovation

Modest performance improvements: Full-dataset gains are small (+1.95% on NYUv2, +1.67% on Occ-ScanNet); Table 4 shows marginal advantage over simpler alternatives (HASSC, GaussRender); improvements appear primarily from pre-training rather than methodological innovation

Pseudo-label quality concerns: Raw pseudo-labels achieve only 10.06% mIoU on Occ-ScanNet; reliance on arbitrary 2.8m wall-height heuristic without sensitivity analysis; limited filtering criteria; no systematic analysis of which classes/scenes are problematic

Unresolved scale misalignment: Addressed only through fixed architectural prior rather than principled method; no ablation on wall-height value; foundation model errors (Dust3R) compound monocular ambiguity without analysis

Weak cross-domain justification: Table 3 shows in-domain Occ-ScanNet pre-training sometimes matches or exceeds YouTube-Occ in few-shot settings; data diversity benefits over scale are not empirically isolated or convincingly demonstrated

Dataset scale ambiguity: YouTube-Occ is only ~2.2× larger than Occ-ScanNet train set; unclear whether improvements stem from scale, diversity, or domain complementarity; no ablation on dataset size or scene characteristic analysis

Overly sensitive design choices: Prototype momentum β (0.999 vs 0.9 causes −1.28% drop) and learnable scale/rotation (−1.76% drop) show brittleness; lack of principled justification or mechanistic understanding
Missing statistical rigor: No confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; given modest improvements, uncertainty quantification is important for credibility
Incomplete analysis of failures: Section 6 lists limitations but doesn't investigate them; no systematic study of which video types benefit most; real-world deployment implications unclear
